examples.title: Header
examples.description: `CodeBlockHeader` holds a `CodeBlockTitle` and `CodeBlockActions`. `CodeBlockCopyButton` copies its `value`. A long title truncates. To link the title to a file, wrap `CodeBlockTitle` in an anchor.

examples.title: Actions
examples.description: `CodeBlockActions` holds any number of buttons. For a wrap toggle, keep the state yourself and pass it to `wrap`.

examples.title: Floating Actions
examples.description: Without a header, put `CodeBlockActions` directly inside `CodeBlock`. The actions float at the top end and stay hidden until the block is hovered or focused. They always show on touch screens.

examples.title: Line Numbers
examples.description: Add `lineNumbers` to `CodeBlockContent`. A string child is split into lines, and the numbers are not copied with a selection.

examples.title: Start Line
examples.description: Set `startLine` to number lines from a given line, for a snippet from the middle of a file. The gutter grows to fit the widest number.

examples.title: Wrap
examples.description: Long lines scroll by default. Add `wrap` to wrap them, which suits tool output and error messages. To let the reader toggle it, see [Actions](#actions).

examples.title: Highlighted Lines
examples.description: Render each line as a `CodeBlockLine` and set `variant = CodeBlockLineVariant.Highlighted` on the lines to call out.

examples.title: Diff
examples.description: Set `variant = CodeBlockLineVariant.Added` or `CodeBlockLineVariant.Removed` on a `CodeBlockLine`. Each one adds a `+` or `−` marker.

examples.title: Height
examples.description: Cap the height with `maxHeight` on `CodeBlockContent`. The content scrolls inside the block. `CodeBlockContent` fades its edges as it scrolls: left and right by default, top and bottom when the block is capped.

examples.title: Show More
examples.description: `CodeBlockFooter` is a slot below the content. For Show More, cap the content while it is collapsed and put a ghost `xs` `Button` in the footer.

examples.title: Max Height
examples.description: To keep a long block from taking over the page, raise the cap instead of removing it. The expanded content scrolls, and the edges fade as you scroll.

examples.title: Size
examples.description: Use `size = CodeBlockSize.Sm` for tool and [Trace](#trace) output. It has tighter padding and smaller code text.

examples.title: Destructive
examples.description: Use `variant = CodeBlockVariant.Destructive` for errors and failed output.

examples.title: Trace
examples.description: Put a `CodeBlock` with `size = CodeBlockSize.Sm` in `TraceCollapsibleContent` for tool and terminal output. Add `wrap` and a `maxHeight` so long output wraps and scrolls inside the trace. The block sets its own text color, so `TraceCollapsibleContent` does not mute it.

Syntax highlighting is out of scope in this Compose port: `CodeBlockContent` renders plain text, and no highlighter is bundled. The official server rendering, streaming and Markdown recipes depend on the same tokenizer and on Streamdown, so they are not reproduced here.

examples.title: Responsive Layout
examples.description:
• Vertical fields: Default orientation stacks label, control, and helper text—ideal for mobile-first layouts.
• Horizontal fields: Set `orientation = FieldOrientation.Horizontal` on `Field` to align the label and control side-by-side. Pair with `FieldContent` to keep descriptions aligned.
• Responsive fields: Set `orientation = FieldOrientation.Responsive` for automatic column layouts inside container-aware parents. A `FieldGroup` switches orientations at the 448dp container breakpoint.

examples.title: Horizontal Scrolling
examples.description: Use `ScrollFadeOrientation.Horizontal` on containers that scroll horizontally. The horizontal fade is direction-aware: in RTL layouts the crisp edge and the fade follow the reading direction with no extra configuration.

examples.title: Edge Fades
examples.description: Use `ScrollFadeEdge.Top` / `Bottom` / `Left` / `Right` for physical edges and `Start` / `End` for logical inline edges that mirror in RTL. Start edges fade in after you scroll away from the start; end edges fade out when you reach the end.

examples.title: Fade Size
examples.description: The fade depth defaults to `12%` of the container, capped at `40.dp`. Use `ScrollFadeSize.Length` to set a fixed size on the spacing scale or `ScrollFadeSize.Fraction` for an arbitrary percentage; per-edge sizes override the shared size. The fade eases in over `revealDistance`, `96dp` by default and independent of the depth.

examples.title: Disabling the Fade
examples.description: Use `enabled = false` to remove the fade. It works in any class order, so the typical use is responsive or stateful.

examples.title: RTL
examples.description: To enable RTL support in shadcn/ui, see the RTL configuration guide. `scrollFade` follows the reading direction: at rest the start edge is crisp and the end edge fades; in RTL that means a crisp right edge and a fade on the left, mirrored from LTR.

examples.title: Color
examples.description: Use `shimmer-color-<color>` to set the highlight color explicitly. It accepts theme colors with an optional opacity modifier, or any arbitrary color value.

examples.title: Duration
examples.description: Use `shimmer-duration-<number>` to set the duration of one sweep in milliseconds. The default is `2000`, i.e. `2s`.

examples.title: Spread
examples.description: Use `shimmer-spread-<number>` to set the width of the highlight band using the spacing scale. The default is `calc(3ch + 40px)`: a fixed base plus a `3ch` term that scales with the font size. For one-off values, use an arbitrary length or percentage.

examples.title: Angle
examples.description: Use `shimmer-angle-<number>` to set the tilt of the highlight band in degrees. The default is `20`.

examples.title: Reverse
examples.description: Use `shimmer-reverse` to sweep the highlight in the opposite direction. In RTL layouts the sweep already follows the reading direction. The official page documents this class with code only; the preview above is added for the Compose page.

examples.title: Play Once
examples.description: Use `shimmer-once` to play a single sweep instead of looping, useful as a reveal when streaming completes. Pair it with `shimmer-duration-<number>` to control how long the sweep takes.

examples.title: Disabling the Shimmer
examples.description: Use `shimmer-none` to turn the effect off and render the text normally. It works in any class order, so the typical use is responsive or stateful:

examples.title: RTL
examples.description: To enable RTL support in shadcn/ui, see the [RTL configuration guide](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/rtl). The sweep follows the reading direction, left to right in LTR and right to left in RTL, with no extra classes. Use `shimmer-reverse` to flip the direction manually.

examples.title: Status
examples.description:
Set `status` on `TraceLine` when a step is running, has failed or hasn't started yet.

None is for work that is done ("Ran pnpm install"). Error is for work that failed; say so in the title ("Failed to run pnpm lint"). Running is for work in progress, written in the present tense ("Running pnpm build"). Pending is for work that has not started, such as a plan step ("Run pnpm test").

examples.title: Collapsible

examples.title: Open State
examples.description: Rows start closed. Use `defaultOpen` on `TraceCollapsible` to start open, or `open` with `onOpenChange` to control a row.

examples.title: Link

examples.title: Dialog

examples.title: Sheet

examples.title: Group

See Sources for more examples.

See Chain of Thought and Task for more examples.
